candidates.name: Recent change frequency with separate churn context
candidates.definition: Count distinct eligible commits touching a file in a declared window; keep changed-line volume as a separate diagnostic, not a synonym. Proposed first window is 90 days with a 180-day sensitivity view.
candidates.formula: F_w(f)=|{eligible commits c in window w: c changes f}|; churn_w(f)=sum_c(added_lines+deleted_lines), separate.
candidates.scope: File initially; function history deferred until reliable identity mapping.
candidates.rollup: Folders use union of touching commit IDs, not sum of file frequencies. Changed-line totals must state that a commit touching several files contributes several file changes.
required_inputs: pinned HEAD and scan content hash
window, merge, rename, bulk-change and exclusion policies
candidates.unsupported_or_missing_behavior: N/A without Git, with inadequate shallow history, or when source/history revisions cannot be joined; do not display unavailable history as zero changes.
candidates.unique_decision_value: Which structurally difficult code is actively costing attention, versus stable code that can be left alone?

overlap.conceptual: Different data source from size/CCN, but large files tend to change more. Churn and frequency share activity information; default to one and retain the other in detail.
overlap.conditional_information_status: Hypothesis to evaluate; no Srcly measurements.

candidates.false_positives_and_gaming: Mass formatting, vendored updates, merges, generated code and squash conventions distort counts. A busy important module is not necessarily poorly designed.
candidates.suggested_action: Inspect a high-activity function/file's latest changes before deciding to refactor. Show the commit evidence and structural components separately.
candidates.implementation_fit: Reuse existing local Git discovery patterns, add a bounded history provider separate from AST scanning; cache by HEAD plus policy. Git --follow is single-file, so do not assume it solves whole-repo rename tracking.

cost.basis: Planning estimate for a bounded proof, not measured runtime or delivery commitment. S=1–3, M=4–8, L=>8 engineer-days; excludes external test-suite execution.

candidates.rejection_gate: Do not make default if no useful new prioritization cases appear in two repositories, history gaps cannot be explained, or bounded local cost exceeds the agreed budget.

candidates.formula: cyclic(v) = (|SCC(v)|>1) OR self_loop(v); compute SCC in O(V+E), excluding explicitly inapplicable edge kinds.
candidates.scope: File/module first; selected package boundaries optionally.
candidates.rollup: Component identity and union of members; summarize cyclic eligible files and components. Do not sum per-file component sizes or enumerate every simple cycle.

candidates.definition: Original method-level Change Risk Anti-Patterns combines cyclomatic complexity and automated basis-path coverage. Line/branch-coverage adaptations must declare their variant.
candidates.formula: CRAP(C,q)=C^2*(1-q)^3+C, q in [0,1]. Percentage form uses q=cov/100; no clipping invalid input silently.
candidates.rollup: Compute per method first; show max with witness, eligible count, flagged count under a named comparator, and unknown count. Never combine max file CCN with file-average coverage.
candidates.unsupported_or_missing_behavior: No scalar when coverage is missing or C belongs to a synthetic/non-executable scope. Optional unknown interval [C,C*C+C] is labelled a bound, not a measured score.

candidates.implementation_fit: Arithmetic is trivial; trustworthy scope/coverage joining is not. Reuse C05 and corrected metrics; no CRAP-first initiative.
